name: ser20
workload: Binary archive serialization using the project's own performance.cpp benchmark (built via doc/CMakeLists.txt), comparing ser20, cereal, and boost::serialization; exact struct/dataset not documented in text, only shown as a bar chart.
claimed_speedup: "Ser20 is sometimes two times as fast as cereal and boost::serialization in binary serialization" (attributed to buffering of small reads/writes to ostreams); chart at doc/benchmarks.png
tradeoffs: Requires C++20 concepts (GCC 10-14, Clang 13-18, MSVC v16/17, AppleClang 15-16); not header-only, needs a separate compile step; API is cereal-compatible except for a namespace change, so migrating existing cereal/boost::serialization code is low-effort; author states it is 'by far not the fastest serialization library out there'.
caveats: Speedup is shown only as an unlabeled chart image (doc/benchmarks.png); no compiler flags, CPU model, or exact numeric figures are given in the README text; the 'sometimes' qualifier implies the 2x gain is workload-dependent; GitHub does not register it as a fork (fork:false) even though the author describes it as a from-source C++20 fork of cereal; small single-maintainer project (34 stars, 5 forks).
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs: WebSearch query "faster than cereal" OR "faster than boost::serialization" github serialization library, and "game networking serialization library 'faster than' cereal C++ github"
